title: Watch mode: auto-detect and load new frames
description:
## Summary
Hot-reload new frames when they appear in the source directory.

## User Interface
- `--watch` / `-w` CLI flag to enable watch mode on startup
- 'Watch' checkbox in playback controls (next to Loop)
- Ctrl+W keyboard shortcut to toggle watch mode
- Status indicator when watching/scanning

## Architecture

### Loading Phase State Machine
Idle → InitialDiscovery → InitialLoading → Watching → IncrementalLoad → Watching (repeat)

### New Resources
- WatchConfig: enabled flag, poll interval, directory
- LoadingPhase: state machine for loading lifecycle

### Race Condition Mitigations
1. File stability check: Wait for file size to stabilize or file age > threshold before loading
2. Incremental only: Don't replace sequence, extend it with new frames
3. Frame number ordering: Insert new frames in sorted position by frame number

## Implementation Tasks
1. Add WatchConfig resource and --watch CLI flag
2. Add LoadingPhase state machine resource
3. Implement file stability checking in discovery
4. Add Sequence::merge_frames() for incremental insertion
5. Add SequenceAssets::extend_frames() for growing vectors
6. Add watch mode toggle in playback UI
7. Add Ctrl+W keyboard handler
8. Add periodic re-scan system with timer

title: Single load section with draggable range bar
description:
Add visual load section indicator with drag-to-resize.

## Requirements
- Horizontal bar below timeline showing loaded frame range
- Different color for loaded vs unloaded regions
- Draggable left edge: adjusts section start
- Draggable right edge: adjusts section end
- Dragging triggers load/unload of frames

## Data model
- LoadSection { start: usize, end: usize }
- Initially covers estimated max_frames centered on frame 0
- Stored in per-directory seaview.toml

## UI
- Bar spans full timeline width
- Filled region = loaded frames
- Empty/dimmed region = not loaded
- Drag handles at edges (cursor change on hover)
- Tooltip showing frame range

## Behavior
- Drag right edge right: queue frames for loading
- Drag right edge left: unload frames from end
- Same for left edge
- Respect memory budget (can't expand beyond limit)
close_reason:
Implemented load section with draggable range bar:

1. Data Model:
   - LoadSectionSettings in settings.rs for persistence
   - LoadSection resource in sequence/mod.rs for runtime state
   - Methods: frame_count(), contains(), clamp(), set_start(), set_end(), center_on()

2. UI Component (playback_controls.rs):
   - Horizontal bar below timeline showing loaded frame range
   - Green filled region = loaded frames, dark = unloaded
   - Draggable left/right handles with cursor change on hover
   - Tooltip showing frame range and budget info

3. Integration:
   - LoadSection now controls manage_frame_window() in loader.rs
   - update_load_section_from_budget() auto-clamps to memory limits
   - Dragging respects max_frames from MemoryBudget

4. Visual Design:
   - Dark background for unloaded region
   - Green for loaded region
   - Brighter green handles at edges

title: Lighting v2: named groups with per-light params
description:
Rework the lighting rig from a single flat NightLightingConfig into named lighting groups with full per-light parameters.

## Summary

Replace the current single-config lighting rig with:
- Multiple named **lighting groups** (each with a visibility toggle)
- Per-light editable params: position, height, intensity, range, cone angle, color
- Group-level generation config (placement algorithm, count, coverage) used only at creation time
- Accordion UI: Groups → Lights
- 2D map with drag-and-drop positioning and ctrl-click per-light visibility toggle
- New TOML persistence format (no backwards compat needed)

## Relationship to seaview-5gx

seaview-5gx Phase 3 (Interactive Lighting Rig) describes 3D viewport dragging of light markers. That is a future enhancement layered on top of this work. This epic covers the data model, UI, and 2D interaction. 3D viewport manipulation comes later via seaview-5gx.

## Reference

See docs/lighting-v2.md for the original design notes.
notes:
## Child Issues

See child issues for implementation steps. Order:
1. Data model (lib/)
2. TOML persistence
3. Accordion UI shell
4. Generation system
5. Wire to Bevy SpotLight entities
6. 2D map interaction
7. Cleanup old system

title: Lighting v2: data model in lib/
description:
Define the pure data model for the new lighting system in lib/lighting/.

## Structs

### Light
Per-light state, owned after generation:
- id: Uuid
- name: String (auto-generated, e.g. 'Light 1', editable)
- position: Vec2 (XZ)
- height: f32
- intensity: f32 (lumens)
- range: f32
- cone_angle: f32
- color: Color
- visible: bool (per-light visibility toggle)

### LightGroup
- id: Uuid
- name: String (default: generation config description, e.g. 'Uniform Grid #1')
- visible: bool (group-level visibility toggle)
- lights: Vec<Light>

### LightGroupGenConfig
Used only at generation time, not stored per-light after creation:
- placement_algorithm: PlacementAlgorithm
- num_lights: usize
- coverage_pct: f32
- Default params (used as initial values for each generated light):
  - height, cone_angle, intensity, range, color

### LightingRig (Resource)
- groups: Vec<LightGroup>
- active_group: Option<usize> (which group's accordion is expanded in UI)

## Rules

- All structs in lib/ — no Entity, no Res<>, no Query<>
- Derive Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize where appropriate
- Methods: add_group, remove_group, add_light, remove_light, toggle_group_visibility, toggle_light_visibility
- Unit tests for all methods

title: Lighting v2: TOML persistence
description:
New seaview.toml format for lighting groups with per-light params. No backwards compat needed.

## TOML Structure

[[environment.lighting_groups]]
name = 'Overhead Grid'
visible = true

  [[environment.lighting_groups.lights]]
  name = 'Light 1'
  position = [-10.0, 25.0]
  height = 50.0
  intensity = 800000.0
  range = 500.0
  cone_angle = 60.0
  color = [1.0, 0.95, 0.9]
  visible = true

## Work

- LightGroupSettings and LightSettings serde structs in lib/settings.rs
- From/Into conversions between settings structs and domain structs (LightGroup, Light)
- Save: LightingRig -> Vec<LightGroupSettings> -> TOML
- Load: TOML -> Vec<LightGroupSettings> -> LightingRig
- Remove old [environment.lighting] handling (or ignore if present)
- Roundtrip tests

title: Lighting v2: accordion UI shell
description:
Build the accordion UI for lighting groups and per-light editing in the environment panel.

## Layout

Lights (section header)
  ▸ Overhead Grid [👁] (group accordion, eye icon toggles group visibility)
    ▸ Light 1 (per-light accordion)
        Position: X [___] Z [___]
        Height:   [========] m
        Intensity:[========] lm
        Range:    [========] m
        Cone:     [========] °
        Color:    [■ picker]
    ▸ Light 2
    ...
  ▸ Perimeter Spots [👁]
    ...
  [+ Generate Group] button

## Work

- Replace existing render_lighting_controls() with new grouped accordion
- Group header: name (editable?), eye toggle for group visibility
- Per-light accordion: sliders for height, intensity, range, cone_angle; color picker; position fields
- Generate Group button opens a popup/inline config (placement, count, coverage, default params)
- Read from / write to LightingRig resource
- No Bevy entity wiring yet — just UI reading/writing the data model

title: Lighting v2: group generation system
description:
Generate a LightGroup from a LightGroupGenConfig using the existing placement algorithms.

## Work

- LightGroupGenConfig holds: placement_algorithm, num_lights, coverage_pct, and default params (height, cone_angle, intensity, range, color)
- generate_group(config, mesh_dims) -> LightGroup: runs placement algorithm, creates Light structs with positions from algorithm and params from defaults
- Reuse existing PlacementAlgorithm::calculate_positions() from lib/lighting/placement.rs
- Auto-name: group gets name from algorithm (e.g. 'Uniform Grid #2'), lights get 'Light 1', 'Light 2', etc.
- After generation, positions belong to individual lights — group does not store positions
- Wire Generate Group button (from accordion UI) to call this
- Unit tests: generate with each algorithm, verify light count and positions within bounds

title: Lighting v2: wire to Bevy SpotLight entities
description:
Replace the existing update_night_lights system with a new system that syncs SpotLight entities from the LightingRig resource.

## Work

- New system: sync_lighting_rig — reads LightingRig, spawns/updates/despawns SpotLight entities and NightLightMarker entities to match
- Each Light maps to one SpotLight entity + one marker entity (if markers enabled)
- Group visibility toggle: when group.visible is false, all SpotLights in that group are Hidden
- Per-light visibility: when light.visible is false, that SpotLight is Hidden
- Per-light params (position, height, intensity, range, cone_angle, color) applied to SpotLight component
- Track entity mapping: LightingRig light id -> Entity (HashMap<Uuid, Entity> or similar)
- Despawn entities when lights/groups are removed
- Remove old NightLightingConfig resource usage from update_night_lights (or replace the system entirely)
- Marker spheres follow same per-light position/height/visibility

title: Lighting v2: 2D map interaction
description:
Add drag-and-drop and ctrl-click interaction to the 2D light map.

## Work

- Existing render_light_map() shows light positions as dots on a 2D XZ projection
- Add click-drag to reposition individual lights (update light.position in LightingRig, sync system picks up the change)
- Ctrl-click on a light dot toggles light.visible (per-light visibility)
- Visual feedback: hidden lights shown as hollow/dimmed dots, active lights as solid colored dots
- Lights colored by their light.color
- Group-hidden lights not shown (or shown as very faint outlines)
- Cursor changes: grab cursor when hovering a light, crosshair when dragging
- Snap-to-grid with Shift held (optional, nice to have)

title: Lighting v2: remove old NightLightingConfig system
description:
Clean up the old single-config lighting system once v2 is fully wired.

## Work

- Remove NightLightingConfig resource (or keep as internal detail if still needed)
- Remove old update_night_lights system
- Remove LightingSettings from settings.rs (replaced by new group format)
- Remove old render_lighting_controls() if not already replaced
- Update NightLightingPlugin to register new systems/resources
- Grep for any remaining references to the old types
- Ensure tests still pass after cleanup

notes:
## Session Context (2026-02-16)

### Branch: spatial-mesh (local, not yet pushed)

### What was done (this session)

1. **Audited loader.rs architecture** — 1396 lines, 0 tests, SequenceAssets god resource with 15+ fields mixing 7 concerns. Mapped full coupling: which systems read/write which fields, how LoadSections bridge Timeline ↔ SequenceAssets ↔ entities.

2. **LoadSection analysis** — GOOD NEWS: LoadSection/Timeline architecture is clean. Pure logic, 90+ tests, UI mutates Timeline directly. The mess is isolated to SequenceAssets (the bridge between 'what should be loaded' and 'what is loaded').

3. **Created seaview-bdz epic (P1)** — Loader refactor: split SequenceAssets, extract pure logic, test coverage
   - bdz.1: Split SequenceAssets into 3 focused resources (FrameStore, LoaderConfig, AssetIndex) — detailed coupling analysis in description
   - bdz.2: Extract pure logic from systems, add tests
   - bdz.3: Split loader.rs into focused module files
   - bdz.4: (P2) Design MeshSource trait for format swappability (GLB/STL/future mmap)

4. **Updated spatial_queries.md research doc** — GLB-first approach: SpatialMesh::from_bevy_mesh() as primary constructor (works for both GLB and STL). Fixed garbled edit artifacts.

5. **Updated seaview-7bw (spatial mesh) epic + subtasks** — Updated descriptions to reflect GLB-first, from_bevy_mesh approach. Notes dependency on bdz (loader refactor).

### Architecture

Key insight from this session: the proposed SequenceAssets split is:
- **FrameStore** — handles, paths, entities, loaded state (read by UI + loader, many consumers)
- **LoaderConfig** — loading flag, materials, coord transform (loader + material system)  
- **AssetIndex** — reverse index maps, gltf handles (private to loader, write-heavy)

This separation enables Bevy parallel scheduling: UI reads FrameStore while loader writes AssetIndex.

title: Memory-aware frame loading with timeline UI
description:
## Summary
Implement memory-aware frame loading with a visual timeline showing loaded ranges. This is critical for handling large sequences that exceed available RAM/VRAM.

## Core Requirements

### 1. Global Config (~/.config/seaview/seaview.toml)
- User-level settings separate from per-directory seaview.toml
- Memory budget configuration (auto-detect or manual)
- Default settings that apply across all projects

### 2. Memory Budget System
- Auto-detect available RAM + GPU VRAM
- Calculate reasonable default memory budget (e.g., 50% of available)
- Estimate frame size from first loaded frame
- Compute max frames that fit in budget: `budget / avg_frame_size`
- Only load frames within budget, unload others

### 3. Timeline UI Overhaul
- Fix: slider should reach 100% (current UI bug)
- Playhead indicator: triangle/chevron pointing down at current position
- Loaded range bar: horizontal bar showing which frames are in memory
- Draggable ends: resize loaded range by dragging left/right edges
- Visual distinction between loaded vs unloaded regions

### 4. Load Section Model (Foundation for Multi-Range)
- Data model supports N load sections (ranges)
- Initial UI only uses first section
- Prepare for future: multiple non-contiguous loaded ranges

## Architecture Notes

### Frame Loading Strategy
- Ring buffer style: load frames around current position
- When playhead moves outside loaded range, shift the window
- Or: user manually positions the load window via timeline drag

### State
- `LoadSection { start: usize, end: usize }`
- `Vec<LoadSection>` in config (initially just one)
- `MemoryBudget { limit_bytes: u64, estimated_frame_size: u64 }`

## Checkpoints
1. Global config file support
2. Memory budget estimation and enforcement  
3. Timeline UI fixes (slider 100%, playhead indicator)
4. Single load section with draggable range
5. [FUTURE] Multiple load sections

title: Unify playback speed: single source of truth
description: The playback speed slider doesn't stick — dragging it causes the value to snap back to 1.0 on the next frame. Root cause is the fragile two-way sync in playback_controls_system (audit Issue 2). sequence_manager.playback_fps (FPS) and ui_state.playback.speed (multiplier) represent the same concept in different units, and the sync heuristic can't tell which side changed. Fix: make ui_state.playback.speed the single source of truth. Have keyboard +/- in handle_playback_input write directly to ui_state.playback.speed instead of sequence_manager.playback_fps. Remove or derive sequence_manager.playback_fps. See docs/audit-visibility-swap-playback.md §4 Issue 2 and §6 Step 2.

title: 3D manipulation system: spatial primitives, camera animation, interactive lighting
description: Reusable 3D manipulation building blocks (gizmo handles, axis constraints, mouse-ray picking, keyboard nudging) plus camera animation and interactive lighting rig. See docs/roadmaps/06_3d_manipulation.md for full design.
notes:
## Design Doc

See `docs/roadmaps/06_3d_manipulation.md` for the full plan.

## Summary

Reusable 3D manipulation building blocks (gizmo handles, axis constraints, mouse-ray picking, keyboard nudging) plus two features that ride on top:

1. **Camera animation** — keyframe-based flythrough paths with Catmull-Rom splines
2. **Interactive lighting rig** — click-drag light markers in the viewport

## Phases

- **Phase 0** — Spatial math in `lib/spatial/` (ray intersection, constraint projection, gizmo hit-test geometry). Pure, fully testable.
- **Phase 1** — Mouse ray + picking (`app/systems/manipulation.rs`). `Manipulable` component, `ManipulationState` resource.
- **Phase 2** — Drag + nudge (state machine, axis constraint override, speed modifiers, FPS camera conflict resolution).
- **Phase 3** — Interactive lighting rig (per-light position overrides, XZ-plane default constraint, seaview.toml persistence).
- **Phase 4** — Camera path data model in `lib/camera_path.rs` (keyframes, spline eval, easing, persistence).
- **Phase 5** — Camera animation systems (keyframe placement, path preview, playback, egui panel).
- **Phase 6** — Polish (undo/redo, multi-select, rotation gizmo, video export).

## Architecture

- `lib/spatial/` = pure math (no Entity, no Res<>, no Query<>)
- `app/systems/manipulation.rs` = Bevy components/resources/systems
- Follows lib/ purity rules per `docs/architecture.md`

title: Architecture: introduce Timeline struct, separate pure logic from Bevy systems
description:
## Problem

The timeline/load section domain is fragmented across multiple Bevy resources with UI state mixed into data structures:

### Current state
- `LoadSection` (Resource) — single `[start, end)` range + `dragging: Option<LoadSectionEdge>` (UI state leaked into domain struct)
- `SequenceManager` (Resource) — owns playhead (`current_frame`), playback state (`is_playing`, `speed`, `loop_enabled`), and `Option<Sequence>`
- `SequenceAssets` (Resource) — owns `total_frames`, loaded/unloaded state, frame handles, entity tracking
- `LoadSectionSettings` — TOML-serializable mirror, also single range
- Pure logic (clamp, center_on, set_start, set_end) lives on `LoadSection` methods — good, but the struct is a Bevy Resource with UI state
- Budget enforcement (`update_load_section_from_budget`) is a Bevy system, not callable standalone
- Frame window computation (`manage_frame_window`) is a monolithic Bevy system mixing spawn/despawn/visibility/memory tracking

### Desired state

**Core library layer (no Bevy dependency, fully testable):**
- `Timeline` struct — owns `total_frames`, `Vec<LoadSection>`, playhead position
- `LoadSection` — pure `[start, end)` range, no UI state
- Pure functions: clamp, center_on, distribute_windows, budget enforcement, spawn window computation
- `MemoryBudget` — already mostly pure, just needs the Bevy Plugin wrapper separated

**Bevy system layer (thin wrappers):**
- Systems extract resources, call library functions, write results back
- UI state (`dragging`) lives in a separate UI-specific resource or component
- `LoadSectionSettings` maps to `Vec<LoadSection>` for multi-window persistence

**Architectural guideline:**
> Systems are thin wrappers. Logic lives in library functions that take plain arguments and return plain results.

### Scope
- Refactor `LoadSection` to remove `dragging` UI state
- Introduce `Timeline` struct owning `Vec<LoadSection>`
- Extract pure logic from Bevy systems into callable functions
- Rewire `timeline_debug` and `debug_loader` to use real library code
- Update `LoadSectionSettings` to support multiple sections
- Ensure all LoadSection/Timeline logic is testable without Bevy

### Related
- seaview-wme: Multiple load sections for non-contiguous playback (depends on this refactor)
- seaview-kz0: Current test coverage for LoadSection methods

title: Multiple named timelines
description:
Support multiple named timeline presets per session, similar to saved cameras.

## Motivation

Users often want different load-section configurations for the same sequence — e.g. one timeline focused on the initial splash, another covering late-stage flow, a third with sparse sections across the full range. Currently there is a single Timeline resource; switching between configurations means manually adding/removing/resizing sections every time.

## Design

- A named timeline stores: name, list of LoadSections (with active flags), and optionally a playhead position.
- Timelines are persisted in seaview.toml under a `[[timelines]]` array (or `[timelines.<name>]` table), alongside the existing `[[load_sections]]` which becomes the 'default' timeline for backwards compat.
- A `TimelineManager` (lib/) holds the map of named timelines and the active timeline name. Pure data, no ECS.
- Switching timelines swaps the sections (and optionally playhead) into the existing `Timeline` resource, triggering `sync_section_loads` to load/unload as needed.
- UI: dropdown or tab bar in the transport row to select/rename/create/delete timelines.

## Constraints

- Must respect existing memory budget — switching to a timeline with more active sections triggers `enforce_budget`.
- Backwards compatible with existing seaview.toml files (single `[[load_sections]]` array maps to a 'default' timeline).
- Follow lib/app split: TimelineManager in lib/, switching system in app/.

title: Spatial mesh: parry3d TriMesh as canonical format
description:
Integrate parry3d TriMesh as the canonical mesh format via bytemuck zero-copy casts. Enables spatial queries (ray cast, point projection, AABB region) on loaded meshes without duplicating vertex data. Adds a Visualization section to the environment panel showing BVH/spatial info. See research/spatial_queries.md

## Updated Priority (2026-02-16)

GLB/glTF is now the primary mesh format. SpatialMesh is built FROM Bevy Mesh (not the other way around) since Bevy's GltfLoader creates Mesh assets before we see the data. The from_bevy_mesh() constructor works uniformly for both GLB and STL.

## Dependencies

Depends on seaview-bdz (loader refactor) for clean SequenceAssets to store SpatialMesh alongside frame handles.

title: Add parry3d + bytemuck deps
description: Add parry3d and bytemuck (with extern_crate_alloc) to Cargo.toml. Verify glam 0.30 alignment with Bevy 0.18.

title: Create lib/spatial with SpatialMesh wrapper
description:
Create lib/spatial/mod.rs with SpatialMesh struct wrapping parry3d TriMesh.

Primary constructor: from_bevy_mesh(&Mesh) — extracts positions + indices from existing Bevy Mesh, uses bytemuck cast_vec for zero-cost reinterpret into parry types, builds TriMesh (which builds BVH internally). Works for both GLB and STL.

Secondary constructor: from_raw(positions, flat_indices) — zero-copy Vec reinterpret for intercepted raw data (future STL optimization).

Methods: from_bevy_mesh, from_raw, cast_ray, project_point, triangles_in_aabb, aabb.

title: Integrate SpatialMesh with loader (GLB first, STL second)
description:
Wire SpatialMesh into the loading pipeline. Build SpatialMesh from Bevy Mesh after frame loads complete (both GLB and STL paths).

GLB (primary): build after extract_gltf_meshes marks frame loaded
STL (secondary): build after track_asset_loading marks frame loaded

Storage: Vec<Option<Vec<SpatialMesh>>> parallel to frame_handles in SequenceAssets (or successor resource from seaview-bdz refactor). One SpatialMesh per mesh primitive.

BVH build (~20-40ms for 2M tris) should be async/background to avoid blocking frame display.

Depends on seaview-bdz (loader refactor) for clean resource structure.

title: Environment panel: Visualization section
description: Add Visualization accordion section to environment panel. Show BVH stats (triangle count, tree depth, build time), mesh AABB dimensions, spatial query availability indicator.

title: Unify frame advancement: fix flickering and stutter
description: playback_controls_system overwrites ui_state.current_frame from sequence_manager every frame (audit Issue 3), which can revert frame advances from playback_update_system causing flicker/stutter. Fix: make sequence_manager.current_frame the single source of truth for frame index. All advancement (keyboard, timer, UI buttons) writes directly to sequence_manager. The UI only reads from it for display. See docs/audit-visibility-swap-playback.md §4 Issue 3 and §6 Step 1.

title: Load section visibility model & budget rework
description:
## Summary

Replace the current hard-budget enforcement (sections get clamped/resized to fit memory) with a **visibility-based** model where sections can be freely sized but only **active** sections consume memory.

## Current behaviour (problems)

- `enforce_budget` runs every frame and shrinks sections to fit within memory budget
- Users can't freely resize sections — drags are constrained by budget
- Budget is enforced by mutating the user's layout, which is confusing and destructive

## New model

### LoadSection gets an `active: bool` field
- **Active** sections have their frames loaded into memory (consume budget)
- **Inactive** sections are just bookmarks — drawn greyed out, no memory cost
- Users can freely create, resize, and move ANY section regardless of budget

### Visibility stealing (budget enforcement via activation)
- **Creating a new section** → auto-activates it → deactivates the furthest-away active section(s) if needed to stay within budget
- **Clicking an inactive section** → activates it → deactivates furthest-away active section(s) if needed
- "Furthest away" = measured from the playhead (the most relevant reference point)
- Sections are never resized by the system — only their active flag changes

### UI changes
- Active sections: drawn with current colour palette
- Inactive sections: drawn greyed out / semi-transparent with a dimmed handle
- Click on inactive section body → activate (steal from furthest)
- Maybe a small eye icon or indicator for active/inactive state
- Remove budget constraints from `set_start`, `set_end`, `move_to` — free dragging
- Tooltip should show active/inactive status per section

## Implementation plan

### Phase 1: Data model
1. Add `active: bool` to `LoadSection`
2. Update `LoadSection::new` → active by default
3. Update `frames_to_load()` → only return frames from active sections
4. Update `compute_spawn_windows()` → only consider active sections
5. Update `total_loaded()` → only count active sections
6. New: `fn activate_section(&mut self, idx, max_frames)` — activates section, deactivates furthest from playhead if over budget
7. New: `fn deactivate_section(&mut self, idx)`
8. Rework `enforce_budget()` → toggle active flags instead of resizing sections

### Phase 2: UI
1. `load_section_bar.rs`: draw inactive sections greyed out
2. Click on inactive section body → call `activate_section`
3. Remove budget param from `set_start` / `set_end` — free dragging
4. Ctrl+drag to create → new section is auto-activated
5. Update cursor/tooltip for inactive sections
6. `apply_drag`: remove budget constraints, keep only neighbour collision

### Phase 3: Loader integration
1. `sync_section_loads`: only load frames from active sections, unload frames from deactivated ones
2. `update_timeline_budget`: toggle visibility instead of clamping sizes
3. Remove hard budget enforcement from drag path entirely

### Phase 4: Persistence
1. Add `active` field to `LoadSectionSettings`
2. Update `From` impls for serialization/deserialization
3. Backwards compat: missing `active` field defaults to `true`

## Distance metric

"Furthest away" for stealing: euclidean distance of section center from playhead.
`distance = |section.center() - playhead|`
Deactivate the section with the largest distance first.
notes:
## Clarification

Deactivating a section UNLOADS its frames from memory — this is the whole point. Active = loaded in memory. Inactive = not loaded, just a bookmark on the timeline.

The flow:
1. User creates/activates a section → frames get loaded (sync_section_loads enqueues them)
2. Budget exceeded → system deactivates furthest section → sync_section_loads sees those frames are no longer needed → unloads them (removes handles, despawns entities)
3. User clicks inactive section → reactivates → frames load back in, furthest active section deactivates and unloads

So the active flag directly controls the memory lifecycle. frames_to_load() only returns frames from active sections. sync_section_loads compares what's loaded vs what's needed and handles both loading and unloading.

title: Multi-vendor GPU VRAM detection and multi-GPU selection
description:
## Summary

Currently VRAM detection uses NVML (NVIDIA Management Library) which only works for NVIDIA GPUs. When NVML is unavailable, we fall back to a conservative 4 GB estimate. This is inadequate for AMD and Intel GPU users, and doesn't handle multi-GPU systems.

## Requirements

### 1. Multi-vendor VRAM detection
Support accurate VRAM detection across GPU vendors:

- **NVIDIA**: NVML via `nvml-wrapper` (already implemented)
- **AMD**: ROCm SMI (`librocm_smi64.so`) or sysfs (`/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total`)
- **Intel**: sysfs or `libze_loader.so` (Level Zero API)
- **Fallback**: Conservative 4 GB estimate (current behavior)

Detection should be automatic — try each backend in order and use the first that succeeds.

### 2. Multi-GPU support
Systems may have multiple GPUs (e.g. integrated + discrete, or multiple discrete cards):

- Enumerate all available GPUs with their VRAM
- Let the user choose which GPU to target for budget calculations
- Global config setting: `[memory] gpu_index = 0` or `gpu_name = "RTX 5060"`
- Log all detected GPUs at startup for visibility

### 3. Architecture
The existing `VramDetector` trait is the right abstraction. Add:

- `AmdBackend` — AMD VRAM detection
- `IntelBackend` — Intel VRAM detection
- `GpuEnumerator` — discovers all GPUs and their backends
- Config-driven selection: user picks GPU by index or name substring match

### 4. sysfs fallback for Linux
On Linux, `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_total` often works for AMD and can supplement other backends. This is zero-dependency and should be tried before giving up.

## Notes
- NVML is now a required (non-optional) dependency — consider making vendor-specific backends optional features if compile times or portability become a concern
- The `debug_loader` binary should also enumerate GPUs when available
- wgpu `max_buffer_size` heuristic was removed as unreliable (reported 4096 TB on an 8 GB card)
notes: Punted: not worth building until we have live users on non-NVIDIA hardware requesting it. NVML + 4GB fallback is fine for now.

title: Memory budget estimation and frame limit
description:

- Estimate frame size from first loaded mesh (vertex count * stride + index count * 4)
- Compute max_frames = budget / estimated_frame_size
- Enforce limit in SequenceAssets

## New Resources

## Integration
- After first frame loads, estimate size and compute max frames
- LoadSection respects this limit
- Unload frames outside the section to stay within budget

title: Loader refactor: split SequenceAssets, extract pure logic, test coverage
description:
Refactor lib/sequence/loader.rs (1396 lines, 0 tests) into clean modules.

## Current State

loader.rs is the oldest code in the project. It has grown into a 1400-line monolith with:
- SequenceAssets: a god resource with 15+ fields mixing 7 concerns
- 7 systems with business logic inline (no pure function extraction)
- Zero unit tests — all logic embedded in ECS system signatures
- Duplicated memory estimation + coord transform caching across GLB/STL paths
- No format abstraction — GLB vs STL handled via scattered match branches

Architecture doc already flags SequenceAssets as known debt.

## Goals

1. Split loader.rs into focused modules (~200 lines each)
2. Extract pure logic from systems into testable lib/ functions
3. Break up SequenceAssets into focused resources (frame store, loading state, format config)
4. Add unit tests for all extracted logic
5. Introduce a trait-based mesh source abstraction (MeshSource or similar) for format swappability — GLB, STL, and future formats (mmap/zero-copy svmesh) behind one interface
6. Design trait boundary carefully given Bevy asset system integration constraints

## Trait Design Considerations

A MeshSource trait would unify GLB/STL/future-mmap paths. Key challenge: Bevy's asset system owns mesh loading and produces Handle<Mesh> asynchronously. The trait boundary should sit ABOVE the asset system (format detection + loading strategy) rather than replacing it. Future zero-copy/mmap format (seaview-joh) would be a new MeshSource impl.

## Module Split Plan

- lib/sequence/assets.rs — FrameStore (handles, paths, loaded state), smaller focused resources
- lib/sequence/load_queue.rs — LoadQueue, drain logic
- lib/sequence/frame_window.rs — entity spawn/despawn/visibility management
- lib/sequence/format.rs — MeshFileFormat + trait-based format abstraction
- lib/sequence/loading_tracker.rs — track_asset_loading, extract_gltf_meshes (or unified)

## Relationship to Other Work

- Blocks seaview-7bw (spatial mesh) — SpatialMesh storage needs clean SequenceAssets
- Prepares ground for seaview-joh (zero-copy mmap) — trait boundary enables new format
- GLB is primary format; STL is secondary
notes:
## LoadSection Coupling Analysis (2026-02-16)

### The Good News
LoadSection architecture is CLEAN. Timeline (mod.rs) is pure logic with 90+ tests. The UI (load_section_bar.rs) mutates Timeline directly — never touches SequenceAssets. The contract is:
- Timeline owns sections (what SHOULD be loaded)
- sync_section_loads bridges sections → SequenceAssets (what IS loaded)
- manage_frame_window bridges sections → entities (what IS spawned)
- frames_to_load() is the pure function mapping sections → frame indices

### The Problem
sync_section_loads and manage_frame_window both take ResMut<SequenceAssets>, which blocks parallel scheduling with every other system that reads SequenceAssets.

### Proposed Split: 3 Resources
1. FrameStore — handles, paths, entities, loaded state (read by UI + loader)
2. LoaderConfig — loading flag, materials, coord transform (loader + material system)
3. AssetIndex — reverse index maps, gltf handles (private to loader)

### Work Order
1. bdz.1: Split SequenceAssets → FrameStore + LoaderConfig + AssetIndex
2. bdz.2: Extract pure logic from sync_section_loads, manage_frame_window, etc.
3. bdz.3: Split loader.rs into module files
4. bdz.4: (P2) MeshSource trait design

title: Split SequenceAssets into focused resources
description:
Break the 15+ field god resource into focused resources.

## Coupling Analysis

What each consumer actually needs from SequenceAssets:

### Loader systems (loader.rs)
- handle_load_requests: resets everything, initializes vecs
- sync_section_loads: reads frame_handles/gltf_handles to check what's loaded, writes to unload frames outside sections, clears reverse indices
- drain_load_queue: reads format/frame_paths, writes frame_handles/gltf_handles + reverse indices
- extract_gltf_meshes: reads gltf_handles/gltf_id_to_frame, writes frame_handles/loaded_frames/loaded_count + reverse indices + memory estimation + coord_transform + mesh_materials
- track_asset_loading: reads asset_id_to_frame, writes loaded_frames/loaded_count + memory estimation + coord_transform + mesh_materials
- manage_frame_window: reads frame_entities/frame_handles/loaded_frames/mesh_materials/coord_transform/estimated_frame_bytes, writes frame_entities/displayed_frame

### UI systems (app/)
- environment_panel: Res<SequenceAssets> — reads total_frames, frame_entities (count), displayed_frame, window_range()
- rendering_section: reads total_frames, frame_entities, displayed_frame, window_range()
- material_system: reads nothing from SequenceAssets directly (uses SequenceMeshDisplay query)
- LoadingState mirror: reads loading, loaded_count, total_frames

### Other lib/ systems
- update_timeline_budget: reads total_frames
- mesh_info: reads nothing from SequenceAssets (uses SequenceMeshDisplay query)

## Proposed Split (3 resources)

### FrameStore (public, read by UI + loader)
- frame_handles: Vec<Option<Vec<Handle<Mesh>>>>
- frame_paths: Vec<PathBuf>
- frame_entities: Vec<Option<Vec<Entity>>>
- loaded_frames: Vec<bool>
- loaded_count: usize
- total_frames: usize
- displayed_frame: Option<usize>
- format: Option<MeshFileFormat>
- base_path: Option<PathBuf>
- estimated_frame_bytes: u64

Public query methods: get_frame(), get_frame_meshes(), is_frame_loaded(), progress(), window_range(), promote_to_gpu(), demote_from_gpu()

### LoaderConfig (semi-public, read by loader + material system)
- loading: bool
- mesh_materials: Vec<Handle<StandardMaterial>>
- coord_transform: Transform

### AssetIndex (private to loader)
- asset_id_to_frame: HashMap<AssetId<Mesh>, usize>
- gltf_handles: Vec<Option<Handle<Gltf>>>
- gltf_id_to_frame: HashMap<AssetId<Gltf>, usize>

## LoadSection Interaction

LoadSections live in Timeline (mod.rs) — pure, well-tested (90+ tests). The bridge is:
- sync_section_loads: watches Timeline.sections for changes, reconciles FrameStore
- manage_frame_window: reads Timeline.sections via compute_spawn_windows()
- frames_to_load(): pure function maps sections → frame indices

This bridge is clean. The refactor doesn't change the LoadSection contract — it just splits the SequenceAssets god resource that sync_section_loads and manage_frame_window currently fight over.

## UI Impact

- load_section_bar.rs: takes &mut Timeline directly, NEVER touches SequenceAssets — no change needed
- rendering_section.rs: reads SequenceAssets for display stats — switch to Res<FrameStore>
- LoadingState mirror: reads loading/loaded_count/total_frames — split across FrameStore + LoaderConfig

## Key Benefit

FrameStore (read-heavy, many consumers) separates from AssetIndex (write-heavy, loader-only). Bevy can schedule UI reads in parallel with loader writes to AssetIndex.

title: Zero-copy mmap-friendly mesh format for instant GPU upload
notes:
## Motivation
Loading STL/glTF files requires: read bytes → parse → build Mesh struct → upload to GPU. Each step copies data. For large simulation sequences (thousands of frames), this is a major bottleneck even with async I/O.

## Goal
Design/adopt a binary mesh format where the on-disk layout matches the GPU vertex buffer layout exactly, enabling:
- **mmap** the file directly (no read + allocate)
- **Zero-copy upload** to GPU (or near-zero — just pass the mmap'd pointer)
- Potentially use persistent mapped buffers or `wgpu::BufferDescriptor::mapped_at_creation`

## Candidate Approaches
1. **Custom .svmesh format** — flat binary: header (vertex_count, index_count, format flags) + raw vertex data (pos f32×3, normal f32×3, uv f32×2 = 32 bytes/vertex) + raw u32 indices. File IS the GPU buffer.
2. **Quantized variant** — half-float positions/normals for 2× density, with bounding box in header for dequant.
3. **Pre-bake pipeline** — CLI tool converts STL/glTF → .svmesh on first load, caches alongside originals. Subsequent loads are instant mmap.

## Key Considerations
- Vertex format must match Bevy's `Mesh` attribute layout (or we bypass Mesh and create `wgpu::Buffer` directly)
- Endianness: assume little-endian (x86/ARM), add magic number for validation
- File alignment: align vertex/index data to 4096 bytes (page boundary) for mmap efficiency
- Could use `memmap2` crate for safe mmap
- Bevy's asset system may need a custom loader that returns a pre-built Mesh from raw bytes without parsing
- Look at: usf (Universal Scene Format), meshopt's quantized formats, Omniverse MDL

## Architecture Notes
- Converter lives in `lib/asset_loaders/` (pure logic) + `bin/` CLI tool
- Custom AssetLoader for .svmesh returns Mesh with zero/minimal processing  
- Existing STL/glTF support stays — .svmesh is an optional fast path
- First-load converts and caches; subsequent loads mmap

## Related
- seaview loading pipeline analysis identified file parsing as async but still CPU-heavy
- This pairs with load throttling (separate issue) — even with throttling, faster per-frame load = better

title: Timeline UI: fix slider 100% and add playhead indicator
description:
Fix timeline slider and add visual playhead.

## Bugs to fix
- Slider doesn't reach 100% (off-by-one or width issue)

## Playhead indicator
- Triangle/chevron pointing down (▼) at current frame position
- Positioned above the timeline bar
- Could use egui shape drawing or Unicode char
- Should be visually distinct, maybe colored

## Implementation
- Check slider range calculation (0..=total-1 vs 0..total)
- Add custom painting above slider for playhead
- Or overlay a label with positioning
close_reason:
Fixed timeline UI:
1. Fixed slider 100% issue - was using total_frames as denominator, now uses (total_frames - 1) so last frame shows as 100%
2. Added playhead indicator - orange/yellow triangle (▼) above the timeline that tracks current frame position
3. Consistent max_frame calculation across playhead, slider, and progress bar

title: Check and fix font size in sidebar
[FUTURE] Multiple load sections for non-contiguous playback
description:
Support multiple non-contiguous load sections.

## Deferred - build on single section first

## Concept
- User can define multiple ranges to keep loaded
- Playback skips unloaded regions or pauses at boundaries
- Useful for comparing specific timesteps without loading everything

## UI ideas
- Click timeline to add new section
- Each section independently draggable
- Visual gaps between sections
- Section list/management panel

## Depends on
- Single load section implementation
- Memory budget system
